## What you should be able to do tonight

- Have someone able to clone the repository, run one command, and reproduce a result you report elsewhere.
- Present the list of remaining lies as the strongest section of the document rather than as an apology.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>50 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Finish reports/milestone-05-platform.md: the event-driven architecture with the read-decide-order-fill-mark sequence, the cost model with components separated and the net-Sharpe-against-cost chart, the test suite described test by test with what each one catches, and the ranked list of lies with dispositions.

## Drill <span class='task-total'>interview thread</span>

Spaced repetition, not cramming. Every drill in the year is collected on the [drills page](../drills.qmd).

::: {.task-list .drill}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> Arithmetic, timed, twenty-third sitting. Ten two-digit multiplications, the sevenths, and 8 percent of 1,250 plus 12 percent of 3,400 in your head.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> Random walks and stopping, combined: a symmetric random walk starts at 0 and you stop when you first hit plus 3 or minus 5. Probability of each, expected duration, and then the same for a walk with steps of plus 2 and minus 1 with equal probability.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> Halfway through the drill thread's second band. Write down the three problem types that are still slowest and compare against your day 91 list.
:::
:::

## The running strategy

::: {.project}
Milestone 5 closes the harness. The event loop, the fill model, the cost breakdown, the point-in-time store and the test suite are the platform every signal in phase 6 runs through, unchanged.
:::
